learning_outcomes.text: Has basic knowledge of matrix theory, systems of linear equations, vector spaces and linear mappings.
Has general knowledge of analytical geometry, knows scalar, vector and mixed products in R^3 space.

Performs calculations freely in the set of complex numbers. Can perform operations on matrices, calculate determinants and knows their properties, can solve systems of linear equations, can determine the number of solutions of a system of equations.
Is prepared for practical applications of learned algebraic objects in technical problems.
Is aware that the knowledge conveyed during studies is not complete (due to time constraints); feels the need for self-education.

syllabus_topics: Auditorium classes are to provide examples and teach how to solve typical problems related to the content presented in subsequent lectures, with particular emphasis on practical applications of the learned concepts in technical problems.

Introduction: elements of logic and set theory. Algebraic structures – basic concepts and examples. Complex numbers: operations, forms, De Moivre's formula, roots, applications. Real and complex polynomials: roots, fundamental theorem of algebra, factorization. Matrices and operations on matrices. Determinants and their properties. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of matrices. Systems of linear equations – solution methods. Vector spaces: definitions, subspaces, basis and dimension. Linear mappings and their matrix representation. Elements of analytical geometry: vector products, lines and planes in R^3.
teaching_methods: Practice method (doing tasks at the blackboard)
assessment_rules: A positive grade from auditorium classes is a prerequisite for taking the exam. The exam is written and covers material from both lectures and auditorium classes. The grade from the auditorium classes depends on colloquia results and activity during classes. Achieving at least half of the points available in the colloquia guarantees a positive grade.
